text: You found a perfect new app or service, offering a free trial! Great! Excited to explore, no commitment. Ready to check it out.
You click 'start free trial.' But then, a prompt: 'Enter your credit card details.' What? It's free! Why do they need payment *now*?
You might think it's for verification, or a sneaky way to charge immediately. You hesitate, feeling tricked. It seems like a barrier before you've even begun.
The real reason is clever system design. Asking for your card upfront creates a small hurdle. This ensures serious users proceed, removing a much bigger barrier later.
When your trial ends, the system automatically converts you. Many people forget to cancel. This initial friction ensures a smooth, automatic transition, leveraging human inertia.
So, next time a 'free' trial asks for your card, you'll know. It's a subtle nudge, betting on your future forgetfulness for conversion.
